title: Spring '26 Release — What Salesforce releases are and why they matter
notes: Post as a thread. Lead tweet should have an image if possible — dark background with 'Spring 26' and the Salesforce logo style. Each tweet is self-contained but builds on the previous one.
tweets:
Salesforce just released Spring '26.

most people click past the notification and move on.

but if you work in Salesforce — admin, dev, consultant, or cert holder — this affects you in ways most people don't fully understand.

let me explain what's actually happening 🧵

#Spring26 #Salesforce #SalesforceOhana

first: what is a Salesforce release?

three times a year — Winter, Spring, Summer — Salesforce pushes a major update to every single customer org on the planet simultaneously.

not a patch. not a bug fix. a full product release.

new features. changed behaviors. updated automation tools. sometimes deprecated functionality.

all of it lands in your org whether you asked for it or not.

why three times a year?

most software ships once a year, or on rolling updates whenever the team is ready.

Salesforce does three fixed releases because they made an unusual architectural bet early on: everyone runs on the same shared infrastructure.

there's no 'Salesforce version 8.2' your company is stuck on. there's just Salesforce. and it moves forward for everyone at once.

the reason this is possible: Salesforce is genuinely multi-tenant.

your org and your competitor's org and a Fortune 500 company's org are all running on the same platform layer.

when Salesforce ships Spring '26, it ships to all of them at the same time.

no one gets left on an old version. no one has to upgrade. it just... happens.

but here's the thing people miss: you get a preview window first.

before Spring '26 hits your production org, it lands in your sandbox.

you have roughly 2-4 weeks to test how the new features affect YOUR specific setup. custom flows, triggers, integrations — you can break them in sandbox before they break in production.

most admins skip this. then wonder why something stopped working.

why each release matters for the people building on Salesforce:

Admins: new automation tools land. Flow gets new capabilities almost every release. things that required Apex last year sometimes go declarative this year.

Developers: APIs change. deprecated methods get closer to end-of-life. new platform features open up.

Consultants: client orgs just got new features. you need to know before they ask you about it.

and here's the part that catches a lot of people off guard:

Salesforce certification exams update with the releases.

if you're studying right now from a course that hasn't been updated since Winter '25 or earlier, some of what you're learning is either wrong or irrelevant.

the official exam guide on Trailhead always reflects the current release. it's free. it's more accurate than any paid course. use it.

what actually changed in Spring '26:

Agentforce: multi-agent orchestration is in. agents can now hand off to other agents. if you're studying Admin or Agentforce Specialist, expect scenario questions about how this works.

Flow: new debugging tools and orchestration features. the 'how do you troubleshoot a failing flow' question just got more nuanced.

Data Cloud: real-time data activation and identity resolution expanded significantly.

if you're studying Data Cloud Consultant or working on any Data Cloud implementation, data governance and identity unification are heavier topics now.

Tableau: Pulse proactive analytics features. Tableau certs may reference AI-assisted insights in data storytelling objectives.

what hasn't changed — and this is important:

the core Salesforce platform hasn't moved.

OWD, Roles, Profiles, Permission Sets. Governor Limits. Flow fundamentals. Sharing and Visibility architecture.

those are still 40-60% of most exams and they barely shift between releases.

if you're cramming: those first. always.

the Winter / Spring / Summer naming isn't random.

Winter release = drops around October (yes, I know)
Spring release = drops around February-March
Summer release = drops around June

the names follow Northern Hemisphere seasons and they've been consistent since the early 2000s.

it's one of those Salesforce quirks that confuses everyone at first.

Spring '26 is live.

if you're holding a Salesforce certification, your maintenance exam window is now open — check your Trailhead for what's due and when.

if you're studying for a cert: use the updated exam guides.

if you're an admin or developer: spend 30 minutes in your sandbox before the production rollout.
